alt: Choose one of three prompts and write one imaginative piece in about 45 minutes for 30 marks: 18 for AO4, communicating effectively and imaginatively, and 12 for AO5, writing clearly with a range of vocabulary and sentences and accurate technical skills.
caption: One prompt from three, 45 minutes, 30 marks: AO4 18, AO5 12.

alt: Three tests for a prompt: can you picture a single clear situation, can you see a turning point and an ending, and does it suit a voice you write well in? A small situation written with precision usually beats a large plot rushed. Narrative needs a change; description keeps plot minimal.
caption: Choose the prompt you can control, not the most dramatic one.

after: ## Structure: shapes that work in 45 minutes
alt: Five structural shapes with small diagrams: a single moment zooming from wide to one detail; in medias res, starting mid-action; cyclical, ending with the opening image changed in meaning; a time shift with one memory; and delayed revelation, withholding one key fact until late. Each piece needs four to six paragraphs with clear jobs.
caption: Pick one shape that gives a focus, a turn and an ending.

alt: A five-paragraph plan using delayed revelation and a cyclical shape, in first person past tense: the phone ringing while the narrator hesitates, the house described through absence, a memory of the last call, answering to a wrong number, and the phone left off the hook so the ending echoes the opening.
caption: Plan shape, voice and ending in about four minutes.

alt: A weak paragraph repeats “scared” and “very” and tells the reader how the narrator feels. The revision removes the repetition, shows fear through physical detail (“I had stopped breathing”), varies sentence length and uses the unusual image “borrowed”.
caption: Show feeling through detail, and let one precise word replace several.

alt: A fast version, “I opened the letter and it said I had failed”, is slowed in four steps: small physical steps, one sensory detail, one thought, then the outcome. A pace strip shows the key moment taking far more space than the faster paragraphs around it.
caption: Spend the most words where the tension is highest.

alt: A 45-minute bar: one minute to choose the prompt, four or five minutes to plan shape, voice and ending, about 35 minutes writing while checking the time at each paragraph, and three minutes proofreading. A prepared bank of techniques is useful; a prepared story is risky.
caption: Plan briefly, write for about 35 minutes, and keep three minutes to proofread.
